security_audit.summary: All five static findings are false positives: the backticks are Markdown formatting, and the hardcoded URL is a documentation link. The skill still introduces a medium-risk capability because generated backend code can send requests to arbitrary URLs without documented validation or allowlisting.

remediation.suggestion: Document URL validation and host allowlisting. Warn authors not to pass user-controlled URLs to the outcall helpers.
Add guidance for protecting credentials and request data. Secrets should only be sent to trusted, approved endpoints.

content.user_title: Add Backend HTTP Outcalls to Caffeine AI
content.value_statement: Backend canisters need a controlled way to call external services. This skill shows how to add GET and POST outcalls with transform callbacks.
actual_capabilities: Explains how HTTP outcalls run from a Caffeine AI backend canister.
Documents the prefabricated Motoko module types and request functions.
Shows how to import the outcall module into a backend actor.
Demonstrates a GET request with the required transform callback.
Identifies POST support with headers, a text body, and a transform callback.
Notes the Motoko JSON parsing limitation and suggests frontend parsing.
limitations: The skill covers backend outcalls, not frontend HTTP requests.
The example demonstrates GET usage but only states that POST usage is analogous.
It does not provide authentication, retries, URL allowlisting, validation, or error handling.
It does not parse JSON responses inside Motoko.

use_cases.title: Prototype a service integration

prompt_templates.title: Create a POST outcall

prompt_templates.title: Adapt an existing backend function

prompt_templates.scenario: Integrate an outcall into existing Motoko code

output_examples.input: Add a GET outcall to a weather service.
output: Imports the prefabricated outcall module in the backend.
Creates an asynchronous request function for the selected weather endpoint.
Provide the target URL, extra headers, text body, and transform callback.
Keep credentials limited to trusted endpoints.
Handle the returned text according to the application needs.

output_examples.input: Can the backend parse the JSON response?
output_examples.output: The skill states that Motoko does not directly support JSON parsing. It recommends sending the response to the frontend for parsing.

best_practices: Keep service outcalls in the backend when credentials or server-side integration are required.
Validate URLs and allowlist trusted hosts before sending requests.
Use the provided transform callback and review response data before returning it.
anti_patterns: Do not pass unrestricted user-supplied URLs into backend outcall functions.
Do not send credentials or private data to unknown endpoints.
Do not assume the example provides retries, validation, JSON parsing, or complete error handling.

faq.question: What request methods does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It documents HTTP GET and POST helpers for backend canisters.

faq.question: Does this skill support frontend requests?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on HTTP outcalls performed by the backend canister.

faq.question: Which Motoko module is used?
faq.answer: It uses the prefabricated mo:caffeineai-http-outcalls/outcall module.

faq.question: Is a transform callback required?
faq.answer: Yes. Both documented request helpers accept a transform callback.

faq.question: Does the skill include a complete POST example?
faq.answer: No. It provides the POST function signature and states that usage is analogous to GET.

faq.question: Can Motoko parse the returned JSON directly?
faq.answer: The skill says JSON parsing is not directly supported. It recommends passing JSON to the frontend for parsing.
